feedback.problem: Calculate, in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{11}{13}$ for $-{180}^{∘}<x\le {180}^{∘}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{11}{13})=-57.795\,772{…}^{∘}≈-{57.796}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-{57.796}^{∘}$ lies inside the range, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-{57.796}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={57.796}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={57.796}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/f204faa6327d057dbea5de66f2c6ffca0a9982c299d1e4278dbc6514ddf016df.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{57.796}^{∘} \\  & ={237.796}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get the second solution ${x}_{2}$ that's within the given domain, we simply subtract ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
{x}_{2}=X-{360}^{∘}={237.796}^{∘}-{360}^{∘}=-{122.204}^{∘}
$$

So, the solutions (rounded to the nearest integer) are $x=-{122}^{∘},-{58}^{∘}.$
